summary: The lecture covers core concepts of Jainism and Buddhism, including Jainism's antiquity, two major sects, rejection of creator God, three jewels (right belief, knowledge, conduct), supreme principle of non-violence, and Mahavira's life. It also outlines Buddhism's Noble Eightfold Path and references Buddha's enlightenment after 49 days of meditation.
points: Jainism is one of the oldest religions still practiced today
Jainism has two major ancient sects: Digambara and Svetambara
Jainism rejects creator God; universe evolves via natural cause-effect
Three Jewels of Jainism: right belief, right knowledge, right conduct
Supreme principle of Jainism is non-violence (ahimsa)
Mahavira renounced at 30, attained kevala jnana after 12 years, died at 72
Mahavira taught karma, transmigration of soul, and non-possession (aparigraha)
Buddhism's Noble Eightfold Path: right understanding, thought, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration
Buddha attained enlightenment on 49th day under Bodhi tree on river Niranjana
Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path constitute core Buddhist teachings

check.q: Which principle is supreme in Jainism according to the lecture?
How many major ancient sects does Jainism have?
What does the Noble Eightfold Path in Buddhism include?
opts: Right understanding, thought, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration
